finding_details.closure: One atomic transition: the exact reservation leaves the table, exactly one cleanup entry is inserted, and the token is marked CONSUMED.  An insertion that raises restores the reservation to the table and to RESERVED, so capacity accounting is never lost to a half-finished conversion.  Any mismatch refuses with CleanupReservationRefused before the insertion, mutates neither the registry's valid state nor the foreign token, and appends a classified refusal.  _release_reservation performs the same proof, so a foreign or stale token can neither release capacity nor be mutated.
finding_details.current_code_path: admissible/paired_runner/private_workspace.py: _IncompleteCleanupRegistry.record tested reserved = reservation is not None and reservation.active and, when true, skipped the capacity check entirely; _release_reservation mutated whatever object it was handed; _CapacityReservation.active was a plain writable attribute.
finding_details.delegated_physical_test: test_a_real_inherited_reservation_is_refused_before_any_fork_or_mkdir: a real supervised path with the registry capacity constrained to one, a real PID/generation reset in a forked child, the child registry filled normally, insertion attempted with the inherited token, and the refusal proved to happen before any fork and before any directory is created, with the capacity not exceeded and the parent reservation coherent.
finding_details.deterministic_tests: ReservationProvenanceTests: a stale token surviving a PID reset is refused and unmutated; a fork-inherited active token is refused in a real forked child and the parent's capability is untouched; a token from another registry instance is refused and the issuing registry is unmutated; a forged token with copied fields is refused; the same id standing for a different object is refused; a token absent from the table is refused; a consumed token cannot be reused and a released token cannot be consumed; a stale token cannot release capacity it does not hold; every refusal is classified in the durable evidence; capacity counts entries and live reservations together and stays hard-bounded under every refusal; eight concurrent consumers of one token yield exactly one entry and seven classified refusals; an insertion failure rolls the reservation back and it is still spendable exactly once; conversion is linear and exactly once; the active flag cannot be written.
finding_details.evidence: cleanup_registry_evidence() gains registry_identity, epoch, per-reservation state and the classified reservation_refusals; each refusal names the operation, the code, both registries' identities and epochs, the token's owner PID and state, and the held count against the capacity.
finding_details.minimal_production_change: Each registry carries an immutable identity and a PID-bound epoch that advances on every fork reset, with the reservation table under the same lock as capacity and entries.  Each reservation carries its issuing registry object and identity, owner PID, epoch, id and an explicit lifecycle state (RESERVED/CONSUMED/RELEASED); active is a read-only property and the class has __slots__, so no public method can make a foreign token appear current.  Under the registry lock, a token that would grant capacity is verified on the exact type, token._registry is self, the registry identity, the owner PID, the epoch, the id being outstanding in this registry's table, the object under that id being this exact object, and the state being RESERVED.
finding_details.refusal_condition: Any provenance element mismatched -- type, registry object, registry identity, owner PID, epoch, table membership, object identity or lifecycle state: refuse before the insertion, classify it, and mutate nothing.
finding_details.reproduction: Capacity constrained to one, at 63df0305861fe8d1f3760c0f9a2083dafc51cdf5: a token issued before a PID-bound reset still reported active=True and inserted a second entry (capacity 1, entries 2), and the refusing registry mutated it to active=False with converted_to set; a token from another registry instance and a plain duck-typed object with the right attributes each did the same, and the foreign registry's own reservation table was mutated by a registry that did not own it.
finding_details.title: a reservation was accepted on the strength of an 'active' attribute, so stale, foreign, forged and fork-inherited tokens each bypassed the registry capacity
finding_details.violated_invariant: A reservation is a linear, registry-issued capability valid only for the exact issuing registry instance, the exact current PID, the exact current registry generation, the exact reservation id, the exact object stored under that id, and one atomic transition into one cleanup entry.
